COPE: Position revised on 13 February 2023: AI cannot be an author. Authors must disclose the tool and purpose in Materials and Methods or an equivalent section, including use in writing, producing images/graphics and collecting/analysing data; humans are responsible for the content. This position does not establish a specific rule for reviewers and does not replace each journal's policy.
ICMJE: The recommendations distinguish authorship, peer review and editing. Authors must disclose use in the cover letter and the relevant manuscript section and verify accuracy, plagiarism and references; AI is neither an author nor a primary source. Reviewers follow the journal's policy or obtain prior permission and disclose use. Manuscripts must not be uploaded to systems without assured confidentiality unless the applicable express permission has been granted. The text includes images within authors' responsibility but does not establish a specific image-permission policy here. The year of the version consulted is not stated.
WAME: Version 2, 31 May 2023. New text: Acknowledgements and prompts, including conversion into tables/illustrations. Analysis, results, figures or code: Abstract and Methods, tool/version, prompt and date/time. Authors are responsible for integrity and must not fabricate data. Editors and reviewers must explain their use; uploading a manuscript to a chatbot breaches confidentiality. This is not blanket permission for any synthetic image.
CSE: Section 2.1.15 updated on 26 December 2025. Recommends explicit policies and annual review; authors, reviewers and editors should disclose the tool and purpose, except for basic grammar/spelling uses. Authors disclose to the journal at submission and to readers, retaining full responsibility. No part of a manuscript or review may be entered into a public chatbot/LLM; editorial decisions must not rely solely on generated summaries/recommendations. Recommends that each journal specify rules for text, images and other uses; does not establish universal image permission.
EASE: EASE recommendations (2024), not automatically binding rules for every journal. Recommends disclosing use in creation/editing, including responses to reviews; methods/data/code in Methods or an AI statement, with visualisations also identified in captions. Each journal should specify whether language editing is exempt. Reviewers should follow the local policy and disclose assistance in creating/editing their review; detectors should not be used as conclusive evidence.
ALLEA — Código Europeu de Integridade: The 2023 European Code, sections 2.3, 2.8 and 3.1: report methods and the use of AI/automated tools according to disciplinary standards; no fixed manuscript section is specified. Reviewers and editors must disclose AI use and protect confidentiality. Concealing use in creation/writing is unacceptable practice; fabricating and falsifying data/images are general breaches.
Comissão Europeia — ERA Living Guideline: Fourth edition, October 2026. Guidelines on responsibility and transparency, without creating new legal requirements. Researchers remain responsible and should disclose substantial uses according to disciplinary, editorial, institutional and funding rules; minor technical correction generally does not require disclosure. In evaluation, limited assistance is allowed only when authorised: it may clarify concepts or language but must not write reviews or assess scientific merit. No universal disclosure section or specific image rule is prescribed.
STM — classificação de usos de IA: Final framework of September 2025, with nine classes of use in manuscript preparation. Distinguishes writing, translation, data/code formatting, illustration, visualisation and references. It neither harmonises nor determines permissions or disclosure locations: these decisions belong to publishers and communities. It does not regulate AI as a research method or provide its own reviewer rule. Identifying a use in the classification does not authorise it.
ISTIC + editoras globais (China): AIGC Guide 2.0 developed by ISTIC with publishing partners; it does not replace each publisher's/journal's own policy. Allows assistance in writing and presenting real data under human responsibility and requests the tool, version, uses and affected parts in Methods or Acknowledgements. Reviewers may use only assistance allowed by the journal, without uploading confidential manuscripts. Fabricating experimental images and using AI in graphical abstracts are prohibited; cover art requires prior permission and appropriate rights. The normative year is not stated in the document consulted.
American Chemical Society (ACS): Disclose all uses; the editor may judge use excessive.
American Physical Society (APS): Substantive use must be disclosed in the article: Methods for research, captions for figures and Acknowledgments for other uses. Light polishing is exempt. Reviewers may organise and improve their own text, with disclosure beyond light editing and with confidentiality safeguards; material must not be submitted to unrestricted tools. Editors use tools managed/licensed by APS. Visualisations must be verified; promotional art is restricted.
American Mathematical Society: Adapts COPE's February 2023 position, without an explicit date for AMS adoption. Use in writing, images/graphics and data must be reported in Methods or an equivalent section, stating the tool and purpose. Human responsibility applies. Editors and reviewers must not upload the article to an LLM in any format or for any purpose; this does not imply a ban on all non-confidential assistance.
London Mathematical Society: An AI Declaration is mandatory, including confirmation of non-use; it covers ideas, calculations, proofs and language, with the tool/model and purpose. Reviewers must not upload the manuscript or delegate its evaluation, but may improve the language of their own already-written review, disclosing use. Editors may likewise improve their own feedback without uploading the manuscript.
SIAM: Version 2.0, effective May 2026. Disclose use in Acknowledgements or Declarations (alternatives), accepting responsibility for all content; grammar checking is generally exempt. Methods/data and code must allow verification and reproduction. Reviewers must not share manuscripts or delegate core tasks; an editorial exception requires permission from the Vice President for Publications and the author. Technical figures require verifiable and reproducible processes.
American Statistical Association: Statement of 8 October 2024 on responsibility, transparency and fairness in the development and use of AI by statistical practitioners. This document does not establish an editorial rule for authorship, disclosure location, reviews or images; it refers to more specific publication guidance. The absence coding is limited to the source examined, not to all associated journals.
Optica (ex-OSA): Generating text with LLMs is prohibited; figures/code must be documented.
ACM: Authorship policy updated on 14 May 2026: no AI disclosure is required for writing; uses affecting design, methods, data, code and figures relevant to the conclusions must be detailed in Methods. Human authors remain responsible for integrity. Review policy (30 November 2023): only improve the quality/readability of one's own review, removing all confidential or identifying information; do not delegate authorship/judgement. The rule gives no blanket permission for any synthetic image.
ACL (Ling. Computacional): Current central policy: AI is not an author; content-generation uses, including rebuttals, must be appropriate and disclosed in Acknowledgements, with verification and attribution. Simple language correction and short suggestions are exempt. ARR also requires disclosure in the Responsible NLP Checklist; code use may be documented in the README. Reviewers read the full paper and write their own first draft and arguments; responsible language or proof assistance is possible, but manuscripts or reviews must not be submitted to tools without privacy protections. No specific image rule appears in this section; consult track requirements.
NeurIPS: Main Track 2026: authors may use tools under their full responsibility; agents/LLMs used as an important, original or non-standard methodological component must be described in the experimental design or equivalent. Language corrections and basic coding assistance need not be reported. Reviewers may use only the LLM authorised through OpenReview, and only for papers specifically eligible for the experiment; not for other papers. Confidentiality remains mandatory. Other tracks and workshops have different rules, including writing restrictions; this is not a universal rule for the whole conference.
ICML 2026: ICML 2026 allows AI in writing/research under authors' responsibility and encourages explanation of relevant methodological uses; it does not prescribe universal writing disclosure. AI authorship and prompt injection are prohibited. Review policy A prohibits LLMs, except inadvertent use in conventional tools; B allows understanding, literature search and polishing in privacy-protecting systems, but not delegating critique, summarising the paper or writing the review. Authors and reviewers are bound by the assigned regime. This policy has no specific image rule.
SBC — Sociedade Brasileira de Computação: Code of Conduct for Authors, dated 28 February 2024, applicable to events and publications organised or supported by SBC. AI use to generate, write or revise content must be made explicit in the work, in Acknowledgements, methodology or a section specified by the template; list tools and uses, including text, tables and graphs. AI is not an author, and responsibility for content and plagiarism remains human. The code defines neither a specific AI rule for reviewers nor a standalone image regime; do not infer permission for these roles and uses.
AGU: Authorship is exclusively human. Disclose the tool and purpose in Materials and Methods or an equivalent section, including writing, images/graphics and data collection/analysis. Reviewers must not delegate the review or submit manuscripts/intellectual property to AI; they may improve the language of their own text and check references, with supervision and disclosure to the editor.
EGU (declaração): Institutional statement of 22 January 2024 on presentation/publication, not all research stages. Recommends human oversight, prohibits AI authorship and requests disclosure in an appropriate section (examples: Methods or Acknowledgements, without a single required location). Recommends not applying AI to assess manuscript quality. It does not set its own image-generation rule; check the journal's policy.
Periódicos Copernicus/EGU (HESS, ESSD, G: Text and interpretations must not be generated by AI; assistive language editing is exempt from disclosure. Figures/diagrams are allowed, identified in Methods or Acknowledgements and certified at submission. Reviewers must not upload manuscripts/reviews or generate comments with AI, but may use punctuation, grammar and spelling assistance. Judgement remains human.
Geological Society of America (GSA): Separate section plus a note on the first page for generated text.
Geological Society of London: February 2026 guidance: stylistic editing is exempt from disclosure; substantive text generation is allowed and disclosed in Acknowledgements. Use in conception or research is described in Methods. Submission requires reporting use or non-use. The integrity table classifies generating data, fabricating results, manipulating figures and writing code for new analysis as unacceptable; do not generalise this into unrestricted methodological permission. Image production requires disclosure according to use, without fabricating evidence. Reviewers must not upload manuscripts to LLMs; auxiliary uses such as grammar editing of the review are allowed with human verification. AI cannot be a named author or reviewer.
American Meteorological Society: American Meteorological Society: author clause adopted in January 2024. Substantive AI use in writing, images/graphics or data collection/analysis must identify the tool and use in the appropriate data, methods or materials sections; human authors take full responsibility. Reviewers must not evaluate manuscripts or generate reviews with AI, or upload any part, even to a tool described as secure. The sole express exception is editing the language and clarity of their own review, disclosed in the report. Do not confuse this AMS with the American Mathematical Society.
USGS: Guidance for USGS scientific products, not a general funding rule. Generative AI, including images, requires transparency and human verification. The page provides disclosure templates without prescribing a section. Specific machine learning may not require a separate disclosure when the method is already described/cited; the page does not regulate reviewers.
IOP Publishing: Text generation requires human review; material use is disclosed in Acknowledgements and, when used as a research method, also in Methods. Routine language editing is exempt. Explanatory images and data visualisation are allowed without fabricating or distorting results. Reviewers may only improve/translate their own report, with disclosure and without uploading any confidential content; they must not assess, summarise or write the review with AI.
AIP Publishing: Manuscript preparation and readability improvements are allowed without disclosure. Use that may affect results or conclusions must be detailed in Methods, stating the tool, version/manufacturer, purpose and rationale. Do not fabricate data or alter images in ways that compromise interpretation. Reviewers and editors may enter manuscripts or reviews only into tools supplied or authorised by the publisher, including when using a local LLM.
Royal Society of Chemistry: Cover letter plus Experimental plus Acknowledgements.
RSE, ISPRS Journal and JAG were checked separately in their official guides, which expressly refer to the Elsevier policy. AI assistance is allowed with human oversight and intellectual contribution; AI authorship is not allowed. Disclose the tool and purpose in a dedicated section before the references, from first submission; basic grammar/spelling/reference tools and accessibility assistance limited to that purpose are exempt. Editors and reviewers must not upload unpublished manuscripts to tools, but may improve the structure/language of their review and search background literature. RSE/JAG explicitly allow explanatory illustrations and reproducible data-derived visualisations, with caption and general disclosure; creating/altering primary-data images is prohibited, while research using AI as a method is preserved. ISPRS refers to the general policy and does not separately detail this regime in its artwork section. No normative date was identified in the guides; 2026 was the consultation date, not the rule's publication date.
IEEE TGRS / JSTARS / GRSL: AI-generated content, including text, figures, images and code, must be identified in Acknowledgments, stating the tool, sections and extent of use. Grammar/language editing normally need not be disclosed, although disclosure is encouraged. Content from a manuscript under review must not be processed in a public AI platform to generate a review. Also check the title's specific instructions.
Remote Sensing (MDPI): Remote Sensing's instructions require substantive use to be detailed in Methods and the tool/purpose identified in Acknowledgements; superficial editing is exempt. The title expressly adopts MDPI ethics: disclosure also at submission, data/image integrity, language assistance limited to one's own review with disclosure and without uploading the material, and a ban on GenAI in academic editors' decisions.
IJRS / GIScience & RS / Remote Sensing L: IJRS (guide updated 29 September 2025), GIScience & Remote Sensing (12 October 2026) and Remote Sensing Letters (14 September 2026) require a statement of AI use or non-use in research and manuscript preparation and refer to T&F rules. State the tool, version, purpose and manner of use; the guides prescribe no single section. The general policy requires rigorous human review and prohibits replacing intellectual responsibilities. Disclosed visualisations and conceptual illustrations are allowed, not fabrication/manipulation of results, samples or diagnostic images. Reviewers may only improve the language of their own review, without manuscript uploads, automated analysis/summary or generation of an assessment. All three guides were consulted separately; inheritance does not follow merely from the commercial relationship.
Rev. Brasileira de Cartografia (SBC-Cart: RBC states that it adopts Elsevier's policy and requires confirmation of the AI declaration at submission. Under the adopted rule, manuscript preparation requires a dedicated section and methodological use requires Methods; basic corrections have exemptions. Explanatory images and data visualisations have conditions distinct from primary images; do not fabricate data. Reviewing: only human-led assistance under confidentiality safeguards, private tools and disclosure in accordance with the general policy. Adoption is documented, not inferred from the publisher.
Rev. Brasileira de Geomorfologia (UGB): An AI Use Declaration in a dedicated section before the references, covering every stage and human checks; basic spellcheckers are exempt. Reviewers must not share the manuscript or parts with AI, but may edit the language of their own already-written review without informing the editor and check public facts. Real-data visualisations and illustrative diagrams are allowed; AI-assisted figures must be identified in captions. Fabricating/distorting data or images is prohibited.
Boletim de Ciências Geodésicas: No specific AI clause on writing, disclosure, reviews or illustrations was found in the full instructions available on SciELO. The journal refers to FAPESP's 2014 Code of Good Scientific Practice, which establishes responsibility, authorship, data integrity and confidentiality, without a specific generative-AI regime in the sections examined. The UFPR submission portal was under maintenance. The coded absence is limited to this accessible normative corpus; it certifies neither the absence of additional instructions nor permission to use AI.
Química Nova (SBQ): Responsible use is accepted with human oversight and scientific reasoning. Disclosure is mandatory in ScholarOne, stating the tool/model and purpose; manuscript disclosure is offered as a possibility, without a fixed section. The policy mentions figures/tables but establishes no independent visual rule. AI is not a co-author; references, data and results must be verified. This section has no specific AI rule for reviewers.
SBSR / INPE: The paper rules for the XXII SBSR, the April 2027 edition already accepting submissions in 2026, contain no specific AI clause on writing, disclosure, reviews or images. They require originality, rigorous data, correct authorship and assessment by an independent committee. The absence is limited to these PT/EN rules; it is neither implicit permission nor an INPE institutional AI policy. The versions differ on the submission deadline, and the English version retains a reference to edition XXI; the Portuguese page identifies the current edition and extension. The edition year was not treated as the rule's publication date.
Ecological Society of America (ESA): Disclose the tool and use in the relevant section, Acknowledgments and submission form; spelling, grammar and general editing are exempt. Images and data analysis are expressly covered. Editors/reviewers must not upload the manuscript, figures or tables to AI; they may improve the quality of their own comments, disclosing this when submitting their review. Assessment and responsibility remain human.
American Society for Microbiology (ASM): Authors: AI only to improve the language, accessibility or quality of human text; not to generate original content without significant human contribution. Disclose in the cover letter; further article details may be requested. Do not use for images, covers, videos or diagrams, with exceptions assessed by staff (e.g. research on AI). Reviewers may improve clarity/tone/translation of their own review, acknowledging use in the form; do not copy the manuscript into AI.
EMBO Press: Use is primarily restricted to improving the style, accessibility and quality of human text and images, with author verification and responsibility. Identify assisted parts and tools in the article, without a general fixed section. Collection/analysis use belongs in Methods; synthetic data require identification in the text, figure and Methods, without falsifying experimental evidence. Illustration and visualisation may be allowed with disclosure and attribution. The review sections consulted require confidentiality but establish no specific AI provision; Not addressed does not mean permission.
ASBMB (JBC, MCP, JLR): In ASBMB journals, AI may only improve existing text; analysis code must be reported in experimental procedures. Assisted writing requires a dedicated section before the references; basic checks are exempt. Figures are generally prohibited, except as a reproducible method or a cover with prior permission. The editorial policy and review page consulted establish no specific GenAI rule for reviewers; this is not permission.
ASPB (The Plant Cell): Scope: The Plant Cell, not all ASPB. The instructions allow AI assistance in content, images, code, data and translation under human responsibility; AI cannot be an author. Disclose in the letter to the editor and in Methods or Acknowledgements. Data images must faithfully represent originals, without adding, removing or concealing features; conditional image permission does not authorise fabrication of evidence. The review sections and expressly linked OUP policy require confidentiality and address conduct, but contain no specific GenAI reviewer clause there; Not addressed does not mean permission. Do not extend this page to the society's other journals.
Society for Neuroscience (J. Neurosci.): The September 2026 instructions allow AI language editing and require disclosure in Acknowledgements at submission. This editing permission was not extended to autonomous scientific-content generation. SfN rules, expressly adopted by the journal, prohibit sharing manuscripts or confidential information with AI. Conditional codes this upload prohibition: the rule neither expressly authorises review editing there nor literally prohibits all auxiliary uses. Image features must not be selectively introduced, obscured, moved or removed; adjustments must be uniform and transparent, preserving the original. These visual-integrity requirements are not blanket permission for synthetic illustrations.
Cell (Cell Press): Cell allows assistance, agents and deep research under human control and Elsevier limits. Preparation use requires a dedicated section after the declaration of interests; basic grammar, spelling and reference tools, and non-use, are exempt. Research AI is described in Methods/STAR Methods and in the declaration. Explanatory illustrations are allowed with caption and declaration; visualisations must derive from data and be reproducible. AI must not create or alter experimental/observational images or generate cover art; general tools are prohibited for graphical abstracts. Reviewing expressly adopts Elsevier safeguards: no manuscript uploads or delegation of assessment, with conditional auxiliary assistance. No explicit normative date.
Global Change Biology (Wiley): GCB allows assisted text development under human responsibility, without AI authorship; it requests a detailed description in Methods or Acknowledgements and exempts spelling, grammar and general editing. The editor decides appropriateness. The title's instructions expressly refer to Wiley confidentiality: do not upload manuscripts, figures or tables to AI; improving a review requires disclosure. General Wiley guidance allows illustration and visualisation with integrity safeguards and restrictions on photographs. Operational rules for each image should be confirmed with the editor; writing assistance does not authorise creating data. No normative-version date is stated.
PeerJ: Policy on the PeerJ portal, expressly referring to the Taylor & Francis AI rule: AI is not an author; disclose name, version, purpose and use in Methods or Acknowledgements. Language editing and translation require human verification, disclosure and retention of original and modified versions. Data visualisations are allowed with prompt records, rights and caption disclosure; generating/manipulating images of scientific or clinical results is prohibited. Under the linked rule, reviewers must not upload manuscripts/unpublished information, analyse/summarise the submission or generate an assessment; they may only improve the language of their own review. Confidentiality also appears on PeerJ's own page. Do not assume every AI application or image is allowed.
Genetics and Molecular Biology (SBG): Disclose use in the cover letter and Statements section; document LLM use in Methods or an appropriate part. Assistive copyediting of human text is exempt, not autonomous generation. The section consulted establishes neither specific image permission nor a reviewer rule.
Acta Botanica Brasilica (SBB): The journal's own instructions allow generative AI only to improve readability and language, under human review and responsibility. They prohibit generating or altering data, results and conclusions, and AI authorship. All use must be disclosed in the manuscript, with tool, model/version and date; no single section is prescribed. No specific reviewer AI clause or distinct illustration-generation regime was found in the sections examined; the prohibition on data fabrication remains. The journal's own page resolves the gap in the historical SciELO-based description. No explicit normative-edition date.
Biota Neotropica: Template declaration in the Ethics section.
IEEE: AI-generated content, including text, figures, images and code, must be identified in Acknowledgments, stating the tool, sections and extent of use. Grammar/language editing normally need not be disclosed, although disclosure is encouraged. Content from a manuscript under review must not be processed in a public AI platform to generate a review. Also check the title's specific instructions.
ASME: Prohibits generative AI in content creation.
ASCE: The normative policy prevents AI authorship and requires reporting whether AI tools were used in manuscript creation or preparation; ASCE may require further details. Its rejection of non-human authors was not converted into a universal ban on assistance to human authors. The page prescribes no single disclosure section. Reviewers should not use LLMs or AI either to evaluate manuscripts or prepare comments; the proceedings instructions repeat this prohibition. No specific image AI rule was located in this policy; that does not authorise fabrication or manipulation of data. No explicit normative date.
IET (livros): Does not accept work entirely generated by AI.
INFORMS: The institutional portal allows AI under human responsibility and requires disclosure in Acknowledgements, stating the tool and nature of assistance. The general review rule allows assistance only if the system does not retain, share or train on content and fully complies with confidentiality. The prohibition cited in the 2023 forum concerned IJOC and should not be generalised to all titles; also consult the specific journal rule. Data fabrication is prohibited. The general source prescribes no specific image rule; the version year is not stated.
Engenharia Sanitária e Ambiental (ABES): The full official August 2025 regulations, linked by ABES, contain no specific AI clause on writing, disclosure, reviews or images. They require originality, reproducible methods, references, mandatory figure provenance and author responsibility, and provide for human assessment by reviewers and editors. The coded absence is limited to these regulations and the SciELO instructions examined; it implies neither AI permission nor the absence of other editorial guidance.
Rev. Brasileira de Recursos Hídricos (AB: Use in generation, analysis or revision must be disclosed in Materials and Methods, with extent, tool and parameters. Recommends the SciELO guide to authors and reviewers, without its own specific reviewer/image rule in the clause. The source contains an incongruous reference to RDBCI, recorded as an editorial limitation.
Gestão & Produção: Authors may use AI in preparation, writing, revision and translation; disclose in the Abstract and Methods; reviewers must not generate reviews with AI; machine translation without human review is not accepted.
NEJM: NEJM expressly incorporates ICMJE rules for preparing the work: disclose at submission, both in the cover letter and manuscript, the tools and content produced; check accuracy, originality and references, with no AI authorship or citation of synthetic generation as a primary source. The image section prohibits introducing, moving, removing or concealing features and requires disclosure of adjustments, metadata preservation and no distortion of the original; this is not a generic ban on every illustration. No specific reviewer AI rule was located in the policy examined, although human evaluation and supervised editorial assistance are described. This normative version has no explicit date.
JAMA Network (AMA): Guidance published on 10 August 2026: research and literature search in research reports, Methods; preparation/translation and other genres, Acknowledgment; data visualisation, caption. Basic grammar/spelling are exempt. Drafting Opinion, Letters/Comments and responses to reviewers is prohibited. Generated/manipulated clinical images/illustrations and audio/video are prohibited except in disclosed formal research. AI peer review is prohibited on judgement and confidentiality grounds.
BMJ: The policy covers text, images, data, audio/video and all genres, subject to the editor's appropriateness assessment. Disclose AI in the contributor section; research use is also detailed in Methods. State tool, purpose and task, with inputs/outputs/verification when relevant. Reviewers may improve word processing and language with disclosure, but must not enter manuscripts or information from them into public AI without assured security. Authorship and responsibility are human.
The Lancet: August 2026 instructions: assistance in article preparation is allowed, with human verification and a dedicated declaration at the end of the manuscript (tool, version, purpose and oversight); research AI belongs in Methods. Basic grammar, spelling and punctuation checks are exempt under the general rule. Exceptions: World Report and Perspectives prohibit AI; Comments and Correspondence allow only grammar/spelling, with disclosure, and no translation, new arguments, summaries or references. Directly generated figures are limited to demonstrating the technology in specific contexts; suggesting concepts is not the same as fabricating a factual image. Reviewers must not use AI in scientific assessment or upload the manuscript or comments, even to improve language.
American Heart Association: June 2026 guidance allows assisted writing under human responsibility, without AI authorship. Disclose use at submission and in Acknowledgements; involvement in research design belongs in Methods. Basic spelling, grammar and reference correction are exempt. Reviewers must not upload the manuscript, attachments or full comments to AI; basic correction built into a word processor is allowed. Creating, removing, obscuring or altering data in research images is not allowed. Editorial infographics may use AI with disclosure, but synthetic examples of scientific data or clinical images are prohibited. AI training in research requires the TRUE-AIM form at first revision.
ASCO (JCO): ASCO requires Methods disclosure of AI/LLM use in Original Reports, Clinical Trial Updates or research, stating tool, version, access date, manufacturer and tasks. Human authors remain responsible. AI preparation is prohibited for opinion/perspective-centred genres, including Review Articles, editorials and correspondence; permission is therefore not universal. Reviewers must not use AI to assess papers. The AI section gives no distinct image regime; general originality, consent and integrity obligations apply, without inferring permission for synthetic images. Editorial screening tools must preserve confidentiality. No unambiguous clause date.
ACP (Annals of Internal Medicine): Scope: ACP/Annals of Internal Medicine, not the whole society. At submission, attest use or non-use of assistive technologies, including LLMs and image creators; if used, describe in the cover letter and manuscript. Authorship and responsibility are human. No modality-specific image rule was located in this corpus; a disclosure requirement does not authorise fabrication of evidence. The rule discourages AI in reviewing and prohibits uploading the manuscript, files, description or review comments to any tool; editors should refrain and notify staff and authors in writing of any use. Reader comments on articles must not be produced with AI. Do not confuse general discouragement with broad permission or a literal ban on all uses. Normative year not stated.
AACR: March 2026 policy: revision or translation of human text must be disclosed in Acknowledgements. Generating new content, including text or illustration, requires description in the cover letter and manuscript; research AI is detailed in Methods. Data integrity and human authorship requirements remain. Reviewers must not delegate scientific analysis, summarise the study or generate criticism with AI. Detailed guidance allows assistance with literature, context and presentation of a human review, with disclosure; confidential material may be processed only in a demonstrably closed environment, without violating rights. The policy is not an absolute prohibition on every reviewing use.
Thieme: A dedicated AI-use statement is mandatory in the manuscript, including a statement of non-use. Generative images, videos and illustrations are generally prohibited unless editorial approval and a dedicated form are obtained; non-generative enhancements must be disclosed in captions. Reviewers may use only disclosed language assistance, with assured confidentiality and human responsibility.
Karger: Disclose LLM or other generative-tool use, including image creators, in Methods or Acknowledgements (alternatives); cite software in references and explain how accuracy was verified. Supplementary prompts/outputs are encouraged. Manuscripts and review information must not be uploaded to LLMs/ML algorithms. Karger uses private screening tools under supervision; decisions are human.
Wolters Kluwer / Lippincott: Disclose the tool/purpose in Materials and Methods or equivalent for writing, images/graphics and data. Do not upload an accepted/published manuscript to AI in violation of rights. Reviewers and editors must not upload manuscripts, reviews or letters, even for language improvement. AI cannot be the sole assessment mechanism; screening/validation automation may support the workflow without deciding acceptance or rejection.
Mary Ann Liebert: The Mary Ann Liebert portfolio moved to the Sage platform in 2026. The historical AI in Neuroscience source redirects to instructions expressly adopting Sage's policy: language, grammar and structure assistance is exempt; substantive generation and methodological AI use are disclosed at submission and in Methods or Acknowledgements. Disclosed representative illustrations and visualisations are allowed, not fabricated images presented as original evidence. Reviewers may improve presentation of their own review, without uploading the manuscript to AI or delegating assessment. Inherited coding is demonstrated for this title and the indicated general policy; it does not certify every portfolio journal's exceptions.
Cadernos de Saúde Pública (Fiocruz): Operational PT/EN instructions: assisted writing for readability/language, with human control and Methods disclosure. Figures, boxes and tables must not be created/altered by AI unless AI is part of the design or method, described reproducibly. The operational review section has no specific GenAI reviewer rule. Editorial 40(11) discusses broader uses; this discussion is not interpreted as an exemption from current instructions.
Rev. Brasileira de Enfermagem (ABEn): Adopts COPE recommendations and refers to WAME/JAMA. Methods must describe use and all prompts for text, adaptations, illustrations or tables. For analyses, results or code, also report in the Abstract, including full prompt, tool, version, date and time. References: AI limited to standardisation. The instructions contemplate illustrations with disclosure, but this does not authorise data fabrication. No specific AI reviewer rule was located on this page.
Revista de Saúde Pública (USP): All AI use or content is reported in the Abstract and Methods; adopts the SciELO Guide.
Arq. Brasileiros de Cardiologia (SBC-Car: The journal's own policy allows supervised assistance and requires disclosure of substantive use: writing, translation and language in Acknowledgements or a specific declaration; methodological use in Methods, with tool, version, purpose and validation. AI cannot be an author or fabricate data, references or clinical cases. Illustrations and diagrams are allowed with disclosure, accuracy and rights preserved; they must not be presented as original data or alter evidence. Reviewers must not submit confidential materials to external AI or delegate their review; assistance limited to their own comments requires confidentiality and responsibility, with substantive use communicated to the editor. The page has no unambiguous normative date; supporting references contain inconsistent links and were not used as third-party rules.
Rev. Soc. Bras. Medicina Tropical: Follows WAME/SciELO; dedicated section before References; reviewers disclose use in their report.
ASA–CSSA–SSSA: Updated on 30 June 2026. For writing, AI is only readability/language assistance under human control; creating/altering original data and results is prohibited. Disclose at submission and in a dedicated section before references, stating tool, version and validation; basic grammar, spelling and reference tools are exempt. The writing rule does not regulate use as an analytical method. Reviewers and editors must not use generative AI in assessment or upload manuscripts to these tools.
ADSA (J. Dairy Science): Rule of Journal of Dairy Science and JDS Communications. Writing limited to language/readability; disclose in Notes. Generated images are prohibited except as part of a reproducibly described scientific method. Reviewers and editors may improve only the language of their own words, without confidential content; they must not delegate assessment or upload the manuscript.
ASAS (J. Animal Science): Journal of Animal Science's own rule: disclose AI use for content, images, code, data or translation both in the cover letter and in Methods or Acknowledgements; AI is not an author. Assisted images require disclosure and must not falsify data. General OUP principles impose responsibility and confidentiality protection on reviewers and editors; conditional use does not authorise delegating scientific judgement or exposing manuscripts to external services. Specific journal requirements prevail over general author guidance.
Rev. Brasileira de Zootecnia (SBZ): Guidelines revised in May 2024: does not endorse content creation; allows assistance with language, fluency and organisation under human supervision. Disclose in the cover letter and dedicated section after Financial support, stating the nature/extent of use. No specific GenAI reviewer or image rule appears in the review and figure sections examined; do not infer permission.
Scientia Agricola (USP/ESALQ): Disclose tool, version, model and source in Materials and Methods when used for writing, images/graphics or data, plus a declaration before references. AI-translated texts are prohibited. The passage consulted does not require a non-use declaration and does not specifically regulate reviewers.
Pesquisa Agropecuária Brasileira (Embrap: On 17 October 2026, the full submission instructions on the PAB/Embrapa portal, including authorship, structure, Methods, Acknowledgements, assessment, figures and checklist, and the SciELO version were examined. No specific generative-AI clause on writing, disclosure, reviewers or images was located on these pages. General requirements cover originality, reproducibility, author responsibility and identification of figure sources. No rule means absence located in this public corpus, not unrestricted permission or proof of absence in every internal document or call. Confirm with the editorial office before submission.
Rev. Brasileira de Ciência do Solo (SBCS: The editorial policies and author instructions published by the journal on SciELO were checked on 17 October 2026, including authorship, disclosure, review, data and figures: no specific generative-AI clause was located across these four fields. General requirements for originality, responsibility, peer review, integrity and data presentation continue to apply. No rule/Not addressed describe only the normative corpus read, not unrestricted authorisation. The journal's own rbcsjournal.org portal could not be read; the conclusion does not cover any additional rules there.
Revista Árvore: The journal's PT and EN page expressly adopts the SciELO Guide as good practice; it does not detail its own AI rule. The preliminary guide of 14 September 2023 requests reporting in the Abstract and Methods/equivalent and documentation in the review, with confidentiality protection. The title's operational requirements should be confirmed; inheritance here follows express adoption, not merely SciELO indexing. The guide prescribes no specific image rule.
Ciência Rural (UFSM): Does not allow AI to write the manuscript, abstract, keywords, hypotheses or conclusion. Allows language revision and image improvement without adding/removing elements that change interpretation, under supervision and with disclosure in an appropriate section. AI integrated into methodology must be described reproducibly in Materials and Methods. The page prescribes neither a single declaration heading nor its own reviewer rule.
Rev. Bras. Eng. Agrícola e Ambiental: The editorial policies and author instructions published by the journal on SciELO were checked on 17 October 2026, including authorship, disclosure, review, data and figures: no specific generative-AI clause was located across these four fields. General requirements for originality, responsibility, peer review, integrity and data presentation continue to apply. No rule/Not addressed describe only the normative corpus read, not unrestricted authorisation. The agriambi.com.br portal could not be read; any additional rules there were not reconfirmed.
Pesquisa Veterinária Brasileira: AI only to paraphrase or improve the author's text; AI translation is not accepted; image and data use is disclosed in Materials and Methods.
Econometric Society: Econometrica's policy allows AI under author responsibility, with verification of results, interpretations, privacy and intellectual property; software authorship is prohibited. The section examined prescribes neither a specific formal AI declaration nor an image regime. Reviewer instructions require independent reading and assessment but allow organising comments and improving clarity and language; the review must reflect the reviewer's judgement. The society uses Refine only after conditional acceptance for technical and expository checks, without training on manuscripts or judging contribution or publishability. No other journal's or Wiley policy was inferred. No explicit AI-clause date.
Academy of Management (AOM): Authors may use AI under human responsibility and must report its use at each stage, confirm verification of results and provide details if requested. For journals, state model and purpose in the cover letter and acknowledgements; for the annual meeting, on the title page. Reviewers may improve clarity of their own text but must not generate reviews or upload manuscripts, figures or data to AI; editors also preserve review confidentiality. The presentation stage includes figures, but there is no separate specific image policy here.
National Communication Association: Guidance for NCA convention submissions, effective in the 2026 cycle; not a universal policy for all association journals. Recommends transparency about substantial uses and checking unit/division requirements; minor corrections generally need no disclosure. Authors are responsible for originality, facts and references and should not enter confidential or personal data into public platforms. No single section or separate reviewer/image rule is specified; visualisations are mentioned among uses to disclose.
AALS (Direito): Targeted search on the AALS domain and full reading of the Journal of Legal Education Editorial Policy/Submissions page on 17 October 2026. The text regulates author responsibility, editorial checking, assessment and images but contains no specific GenAI clause on writing, disclosure, reviewers or figure generation. The AALS interview about Berkeley's classroom policy is another institution's opinion/account, not an AALS editorial rule. NL retained: no general institutional AI-publication policy was located in the corpus examined; neither universal absence nor implicit permission is asserted.
CSWE (Serviço Social): Rule of the Journal of Social Work Education, not all CSWE. The journal expressly adopts Taylor & Francis's author policy, including article disclosure and conceptual images without fabricated results. Its own reviewer guidance requires agreement not to use AI in reviewing.
Emerald: Emerald prohibits creating new text with AI, including abstracts and literature reviews, but allows editing and translating existing human work. Generative use is described in Methods and Acknowledgements or an appropriate section, with tool and version; the grammar exemption concerns non-generative tools. Reviewers must not upload manuscripts to AI, assess them with it or delegate decisions; they may only improve the language of their own review, disclosing this to the editor. Conceptual illustrations and visualisations of human data are allowed with identification, accuracy and rights preserved; synthetic factual images and cover art are prohibited. Consultation dates were not treated as normative dates.
Edward Elgar: Rule for books/chapters: does not allow writing, rewriting or paraphrasing with GenAI; limited language checkers are allowed. Use beyond minor assistance must be disclosed in the proposal, checklist and manuscript when required. Do not include generated images without prior discussion with the editor; fabricating/manipulating original data or images is prohibited. The page establishes no specific AI reviewer rule. No explicit normative date.
RAE (FGV EAESP): RAE states adoption of Emerald's policy. Generating text parts (including abstracts/reviews), results or statistical reporting with AI is prohibited; editing human text for readability is allowed. Disclose uses in Methods and Acknowledgements or an appropriate section, with tool/version. Generated images are prohibited. Do not use AI in reviewing, assessment or decisions, or upload manuscripts/reviews for editing. Classification is limited to the rule expressly adopted by RAE.
Revista de Economia Política: Disclose at submission LLM use in writing, images or data.
American Psychological Association: Page created in November 2023 and updated in August 2025. The general rule requests disclosure and citation in Methods; detailed guidance distinguishes Introduction, Methods, author note or figure section according to use, subject to editor requirements. Authors verify information and references and preserve records and prompts. Editors and reviewers must not enter submitted materials into generative AI because of confidentiality. The guidance contemplates figure creation/editing with disclosure, without waiving validation or authorising data fabrication.
AERA: Targeted AERA-domain search and checking on 17 October 2026 of the rules linked by its publications page: Code of Ethics (2011), especially reporting/data, authorship, publication and reviewers, and Publications Manual (2021). These documents establish responsibility, integrity and confidentiality but provide no contemporary specific GenAI rule across the four fields. The February 2026 AERA news item on AERA Open editors' views describes ambiguity about ethical use without establishing a general association policy. NL retained: institutional AI policy not located in this corpus, not universal absence; check the journal. NIH rules publicised by AERA are not AERA editorial rules.
American Association of Geographers: Code of professional ethics: geographers should acknowledge, carefully document and justify how and why they used AI in research, teaching, proposals and correspondence. The rule prescribes neither a single manuscript section nor specific AI reviewer or synthetic-image instructions. Research responsibility, privacy and confidentiality remain mandatory; consult the journal for additional editorial requirements.
American Historical Association: No specific institutional AI-publication policy was located after a targeted search and reading of the Statement on Standards of Professional Conduct, revised January 2023. It requires evidence integrity, authorship attribution, acknowledgement of assistance and responsible assessment, but does not codify AI across the four fields examined. Teaching AI guidance does not establish an editorial rule, and historical news of a committee does not confirm its current status. The conclusion is limited to official documentation consulted: not universal absence or permission, and no substitute for American Historical Review or other journal instructions.
Current Anthropology / AAA: Rule of Current Anthropology, not all AAA: disclose tools, versions, period, tasks and supervision in Methods and in the AI Tools subsection of references. AI-generated images are not accepted. Reviewers must not assess or write with AI, or upload manuscripts or reviews to LLMs; editing/translation in integrated word-processing tools is allowed.
American Sociological Association: The current Ethics page (indicated update: 5 October 2025) refers to the June 2018 Code of Ethics. Research/data (12), plagiarism (13), authorship (14), publication/editing (15), confidentiality and review (10/16) were examined: they require human responsibility, prohibit data fabrication and protect confidentiality, but contain no specific AI rule for writing, disclosure, reviewing or generating images. Absence is verified in this code, not in every ASA journal or activity; do not automatically attribute Sage's policy to the society. The AI-rule date remains unknown.
APSA / AJPS: Policy of the American Journal of Political Science, a Midwest Political Science Association journal published by Wiley; not a general APSA rule. Updated 11 August 2026. A consolidated footnote declaration must reflect the submission questionnaire and identify tool, task and oversight; minimal non-generative uses are exempt. Failure to disclose may lead to rejection. Reviewers do not upload manuscripts to AI but may organise ideas and improve their own text without confidential content, and must disclose writing assistance. Images are among uses to disclose, without a specific permission rule on this page.
American Philosophical Association: After targeted official searching and reading of the statement on good publishing practices, approved February 2022, no specific institutional AI rule for authors, disclosure, reviewers or images was located. The statement requires editorial transparency, assessment through professional judgement, conflict management and compliance with journal instructions. This documentary limit was converted into neither permission nor universal absence. The philosophical APA is not the psychological association; no publisher or journal rule was automatically attributed to the society.
AAR / SBL: An aggregated, heterogeneous record. Positive codes refer to AAR's June and November 2026 meetings: disclose in the proposal, at submission, all AI-generated content (text, images, data, etc.); editing requires no citation. Authors are responsible for originality, accuracy and attribution; each unit may reject AI-assisted proposals. This also applies to full papers and presentations, not just abstracts. The manual does not define reviewer use. For SBL Press, the proposal guide, Peer-Review Policy and figure guide were read: this corpus has no specific AI clause; general review, rights and figure rules are not implicit permission. No joint policy is demonstrated and there is no automatic extension to SBL journals.
University of Chicago Press (livros): Books rule updated on 22 June 2026; journals have their own rules. Prohibits using AI to write/rewrite text or generate arguments; auxiliary research and superficial grammar correction are allowed. Report all use to the editor at submission and to readers in the book, normally in Acknowledgements and/or notes. Prohibits fabricating/altering illustrations, including redrawing maps, enlarging image files or adding/removing elements; visualising one's own data is allowed with disclosure. Requires unassisted reviews and prohibits uploading manuscripts, proposals or one's own review to AI, even if the tool promises not to retain data.
University of Texas Press: May 2025 policy: does not accept work with 5% or more of its total word count written/generated by AI. Authors must notify the editor when agreeing to submit for review and include a statement at the beginning of the work describing uses in text, images, graphs and tables; each use must be cited. Generated images require prior Press approval. Individual journals may have their own guidelines. The page establishes no AI-use reviewer rule.
Rev. Brasileira de Ciências Sociais (ANP: Does not accept chatbots or AI in producing texts.
Rev. Brasileira de Educação (ANPEd): No specific AI clause on writing, disclosure, peer review or images was located in the full Portuguese and English instructions available on SciELO. They require originality, rigour, effective author participation, source attribution and identification of graph/image provenance. No rule/Not addressed coding is limited to these accessible instructions, without asserting the absence of additional rules or authorising AI use. The generic reference to COPE was not treated as automatic adoption of every subsequent policy.
Educação & Sociedade (CEDES): Does not accept texts produced by generative AI. Auxiliary uses such as images, references and translation must be disclosed at the end of the article, identifying affected parts, without a mandatory section heading. The clause examined has no specific reviewer rule.
Revista Brasileira de História (ANPUH): ANPUH Editors' Forum guidelines: disclose at submission and in the abstract/methods/note; concealment may lead to retraction; reviewers report use and do not share texts.
Psicologia: Reflexão e Crítica: The journal's own editorial-policy link leads to Springer policies, whose AI section establishes risk-based assessment for authors, reviewers and editors. Assistive use is allowed; interpretive use requires oversight, verification and transparency. Judgement must not be delegated, data fabricated or photorealistic deepfakes created. Reviewers do not submit content to public/insecure AI. No universal disclosure section or explicit normative date. Inheritance was checked through the title's referral; consult its own instructions.
Modern Language Association (MLA): MLA Book Publications programme policy: AI cannot be an author; all AI-generated content—text, images, data or otherwise—must be fully identified in the manuscript at submission, with no fixed section indicated. Authors are responsible for originality, accuracy, attribution and permissions. Images also depend on editorial selection/review and appropriate rights. The AI, submission and image pages examined establish no specific reviewer-use rule; Not addressed is not authorisation. This books rule does not establish PMLA's or other publications' operational policy.
Linguistic Society of America (PLSA): Rule of Proceedings of the Linguistic Society of America, not all LSA publications. Disclose text/translation in Acknowledgements or a note, data in Methods and images in captions, with tool, version, dates and description; minimal non-generative uses are exempt. Reviews must result from the reviewer's writing and judgement; assistance is limited to minimal non-generative correction. Manuscripts and reviews must not be shared with AI; the page itself requests prior consultation with the editor about sharing.
College Art Association (CAA): On 17 October 2026, CAA's The Art Bulletin and Art Journal submission pages, preparation instructions also applicable to Art Journal Open, and conflict-of-interest/confidentiality rule were read. They regulate originality, anonymity, citations, rights and images but do not explicitly set their own GenAI regime across the four fields. Targeted CAA-domain searching did not identify a general institutional policy applicable to all publications. NL retained: a survey limitation, not proof of absence or permission. Art Journal's reference to the T&F submission portal was not treated as automatic adoption of all publisher rules.
DELTA (Linguística): The journal's own submission policy: authors must ensure originality and contribution and make the extent of AI involvement explicit. Generation, analysis or any other use must be reported in Materials and Methods. In reviewing, AI may assist identification of plagiarism, inconsistencies and technical aspects without replacing human decisions. Personal data must comply with privacy and anonymisation guidelines. No specific image rule or explicit normative date is established.
Rev. Brasileira de Linguística Aplicada: AI as assistance in writing, revision and illustrations; not recommended for analysis; mandatory declaration (ANPOLL/CNPq template); ZeroGPT may be used; reviewers must not copy excerpts.
Alfa: Revista de Linguística (UNESP): Right and freedom to use AI with attribution; follows the SciELO Guide (Abstract plus Methods).
Elsevier: Manuscript preparation: dedicated declaration; AI as a method: detailed Methods description. Basic corrections and accessibility have exemptions. Allows explanatory images disclosed in captions and the general declaration, and reproducible data-derived visualisations; prohibits fabricating primary data/images and using general GenAI in graphical abstracts. Reviewers may use only human-controlled assistance and private tools, with confidentiality and disclosure except for basic checks.
Springer Nature: In the Nature Portfolio policy consulted, a risk-based framework: assistive uses are allowed; interpretive uses require oversight, verification and transparency. Delegating judgement or presenting fabricated reasoning/data as human is prohibited. Reviewers may obtain assistance but must not upload content to public or insecure AI or delegate critique. Photorealistic deepfakes are prohibited. This page has no single disclosure location or explicit normative date. Confirm the specific journal's instructions.
Wiley: Responsible use as assistance, not a substitute for human judgement. Substantial use, development or translation must be disclosed at submission and integrated into the manuscript; spelling, grammar and general editing are exempt. Illustrations and visualisations are possible, with photograph restrictions; confirm details and the title's rule. Reviewers may only improve clarity/language of their own review, disclosing this to the editor, without uploading manuscripts, figures or tables or delegating assessment.
Taylor & Francis: Disclose tool, version, purpose and use in the article; each title's instructions may impose further limits. Allows visualisations and conceptual illustrations; prohibits fabrication/manipulation of scientific results, samples and diagnostic images. Reviewers must not analyse/summarise or generate reviews with AI or upload manuscripts; only improve the language of their review.
SAGE: Language/structure assistance is exempt from disclosure by authors and reviewers. Generative use requires disclosure at submission and in Methods or Acknowledgements. Visualisations and representative illustrations are allowed, not falsified data/images. Human review must not be replaced or manuscripts uploaded to GenAI; writing assistance for one's own review does not authorise automatic assessment.
Oxford University Press: Author policy updated on 13 July 2026; the journal's own requirements prevail. Substantial uses, translation, code and visualisation generally require disclosure in the cover letter and Acknowledgements, also in Methods when part of the method, with tool, version, purpose and oversight. Simple language correction and reference formatting are exempt. Illustrations and graphical abstracts may be allowed with disclosure; fabrication of results or creation/alteration of factual scientific images is prohibited. General principles require responsibility and confidentiality from authors, reviewers and editors; check the title's specific review instructions.
Cambridge University Press: Authors must disclose and explain AI use, not list it as an author, ensure integrity, attribution and originality, and comply with additional journal requirements. The general page prescribes neither a universal disclosure section nor a specific image rule. In reviewing, sharing manuscripts or proposals with LLMs is a confidentiality breach and misconduct; title-specific policies may be stricter.
De Gruyter Brill: September 2026: does not accept AI-generated works; human authors are responsible for content. Substantive AI contribution must be disclosed; methods/design: Acknowledgements; simple proofreading/copyediting are exempt. Lawful illustrations and covers are allowed, disclosed at submission; fabricating/altering original data, figures and experimental images is prohibited. Reviewers must not upload the manuscript or parts to AI; assessment is exclusively human responsibility.
MDPI: Substantive GenAI must be disclosed at submission, detailed in Materials and Methods and identified in Acknowledgements. Grammar, structural and spelling editing and formatting are exempt. Generated graphics/content are allowed under integrity and human responsibility, without fabricating or manipulating original data/images. Reviewers: assistance limited to writing quality, with disclosure; never upload manuscripts, figures, tables or communications. Academic editors must not use GenAI in review or editorial decisions.
Frontiers: Generated text must be disclosed in Acknowledgements; AI-produced/edited textual or visual content also in Methods when relevant, with tool, version, model and source. Figures are allowed subject to verification of fidelity to data and absence of plagiarism; supplementary preservation of prompts and outputs is recommended. Manuscripts must not be uploaded to external tools. Reviewers have secure internal assistance, without delegating editorial decisions; any external use requires discussion, prior approval and disclosure to authors.
PLOS: Allows research and writing assistance, with human responsibility and no data fabrication. Disclose tool, purpose, affected parts and validation in Methods, Acknowledgements or the relevant caption. Language correction/rephrasing and cover-letter preparation are exempt from disclosure; translation disclosure is recommended, not mandatory. Reviewers and editors do not upload submissions or confidential summaries to AI or use it to summarise or assess the manuscript; general or language assistance without confidential content is possible and must be disclosed in the review/decision. Illustrative images are allowed with caption and validation, without misrepresenting primary results.
F1000Research: Responsible AI assistance is allowed with human verification, security and rights preserved; it must not replace researchers' core responsibilities. Disclose any use in Methods or Acknowledgements, with full name, version, purpose and manner of use. Prohibits generation/manipulation of original images, figures and data; the rule includes graphs, tables and other representations. Reviewers may only improve the language of their own review and should not upload files, images or manuscript information to AI tools. Assessment and its integrity remain human.
Science (AAAS): The September 2026 table distinguishes tasks: writing or translating content requires Acknowledgements with model and version; code that changes functionality and data generation or analysis are described in Methods. Literature search, language editing and formatting without functional changes are exempt. The general policy requests a cover letter and the relevant section. AI-generated or altered illustrative figures are prohibited without an editor's exception; editing results visualisations requires disclosure. Reviewers may refine their wording in a system without retention/training and disclose tool and use, never uploading the manuscript. The table also prohibits uploading a review to generate a response and uploading the manuscript to AI during revision; language refinement of the response has its own conditions.
PNAS: Research use: disclose tool and version in Methods or, if that section is absent, in Acknowledgements. AI images only when they are the study subject or authorised by the editorial office; not accepted for covers. The section describes assisted editorial screening but gives no general permission to external reviewers.
Royal Society (periódicos): For writing, AI only for language and readability, with disclosure including language editing. It must not replace insights, analysis/interpretation or conclusions. Code/method searches and protein-structure prediction are allowed. The declaration must appear in the manuscript and published work, without a fixed section; this page establishes no specific reviewer or image rule.
Anais da Academia Brasileira de Ciências: In its specific AI section, consulted in PT and EN on 17 October 2026, the journal states that it is studying which uses/contexts will be allowed in order to update its editorial policy. This neither grants unrestricted content-generation permission nor specifies disclosure location, reviewer use or images. Absence coding is limited to the published policy examined.
SBPC: Absence verified only in the ten-page Work Submission Rules for the 78th Annual Meeting (2026): no specific AI rule on writing, disclosure, reviewers or images. The document requires author responsibility, co-author consent, rigorous revision and respect for figure rights; this is not implicit AI permission. Do not extrapolate to all SBPC publications or future meetings. The year identifies the event edition, not an AI-rule date.
SciELO (rede): Preliminary guide of 14 September 2023: disclose use in the Abstract and Methods or equivalent; human authorship and responsibility. Reviewers and editors should document use and not upload confidential manuscripts to services with leakage risk. Each journal's own instructions must be checked; the guide prescribes no specific image rule.
CNPq (Portaria 2.664/2026): Research-integrity guidelines for CNPq-supported research, updated 13 March 2026: disclose the GenAI tool and purpose at any stage—conception, writing, analysis or submission—in the corresponding texts and electronic presentations. Presenting GenAI-generated content as human-authored is prohibited; researchers are fully responsible for plagiarism, inaccuracies and data integrity. For reviews, clause I.e prohibits entering third-party projects into tools; it is neither a textual ban on all assistance nor permission to delegate assessment. The complementary Committees page discourages GenAI in preparing reviews. No specific AI-generated-image clause was located in the guidelines; general integrity and transparency duties apply. The full Official Gazette text was not retrieved; this description is limited to accessible official guidelines, not a full transcription of the Ordinance.
NIH: NOT-OD-25-132, dated 17 July 2025, effective for submissions from 25 September 2025: proposals or sections substantially developed by AI are not considered applicants' original ideas; limited assistance may be appropriate, with no defined percentage threshold. This is not an article-writing rule. NOT-OD-23-149, dated 23 June 2023, prohibits generative AI to analyse/formulate proposal reviews; accessibility exceptions require prior consultation with the federal official. These sources prescribe neither an author-disclosure location nor a specific image policy.
NSF: Notice of 14 December 2023: applicants are encouraged to report AI use in the project description, without a general dedicated-section requirement. Reviewers must not upload proposals, reviews or records to unapproved tools; they may use public information. The consulted page does not establish the previously attributed 2026 update date.
UKRI: Applicants should be transparent about substantive use; translation, improving English and minimal formatting are exempt from disclosure. Generating a proposal/sections without human involvement and using AI in interviews are prohibited. Assessors may only refine the language of their own review, without entering proposals or personal data or asking AI to understand, summarise or evaluate them.
ERC: Assessors must not summarise, assess or draft with AI.
DFG: Guidance approved in December 2025, published/released in 2026. In proposal assessment, AI may only assist: judgement and recommendations remain human. Requires consent from those involved, confidentiality and local, institutional or cloud systems with contractual guarantees and settings preventing improper retention/training. Disclose purpose and extent of assistance to DFG; technical correction without scientific effect is exempt. Review responsibility and validation are personal. The record does not classify authorial article writing or a specific image policy.
MOST (China): December 2023 MOST Guide, a primary ministerial source: allows responsible GenAI use in research and processing text, data and images under integrity, confidentiality and intellectual-property rules. Direct generation of project application materials is not allowed. Generated content, especially facts and arguments, must be identified and its process explained; AI-produced references must not be used without verification. AI cannot be a co-author; disclose uses and details in Methods, an appendix or a relevant location, with name, version and time of use. Assessors need the organiser's prior consent and must prevent leakage; this is not general permission for automated reviews. Images must not conceal, remove or distort primary data, or replace experimental evidence with external images. Writing coding does not remove the specific proposal prohibition.
Wenner-Gren Foundation: Policy of 19 March 2025. Applicants are strongly encouraged to disclose use in a confidential proposal section invisible to reviewers, with tools, prompts and verification; not a general obligation. Reviewers must not upload proposals, review drafts, notes or assessments to GenAI, even with a no-training promise, or attempt to detect applicant use. No specific image rule on this page.
FAPESP / CAPES / FAPEG: Aggregate preserved, without a demonstrated joint policy. FAPESP: 2014 good-practice code, sections 3.1–3.5 on research, authorship, data and reviews. CAPES: consolidated Ordinance 24/2025 (amended by 354/2025), especially article 8, requires quality and confidentiality; the 2025 AI discussion paper states it does not necessarily represent CAPES and is not a rule. FAPEG: consolidated RN1/2008 on committees (articles 4–10), publication duties in RN1/2024 and amendment 3/2026, with an index updated September 2026. No specific clauses across the four AI fields were located in these corpora or targeted official searches. NL proves neither absence in calls, internal guidance or later rules nor authorised use. Check each agency and call without automatically importing CNPq's rule.
